core.title: Route each JTBD step to its layer(s) and canonical call sequence
core.given: A JTBD step (define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, resolve, conclude) appears in work being planned, in any artifact, with or without existing routing
core.when: the step is declared, assigned or reviewed
core.then: Declare for every JTBD step its primary architecture layer(s) and its canonical ordered call sequence of layer.operation tokens across the stack's layer roles, exactly as in the canonical step table.
prefer: execute [domain, application]: presentation.command → application.use_case → domain.mutate → integration.persist
monitor [presentation]: presentation.query → application.query → integration.read → application.aggregate → presentation.display
resolve [application]: application.event → application.use_case → domain.policy → integration.call_external → integration.persist
conclude [integration, application]: application.use_case → domain.validate → integration.persist → integration.archive
Write sequences as ordered layer.operation tokens so steps are mechanically routable.
avoid: Leaving any step without primary layer(s) or call sequence.
Reordering, dropping or inventing tokens versus the step's canonical sequence.
Layer names outside the stack's canonical layer roles.
Adding extra steps to the taxonomy to fit a sequence instead of routing via the table.
core.why: Binding steps to layers and call sequences keeps the JTBD taxonomy minimal yet routable, so a step can be mechanically placed into the layered architecture.
evidence: Every JTBD step declared in any artifact lists its primary layer(s) matching the canonical layers-by-step table.
Every declared call sequence matches the canonical sequence-by-step table for that step token-for-token and in order.

Worked check: define → layers [domain], sequence [presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.create, integration.persist]; monitor → layers [presentation], sequence [presentation.query, application.query, integration.read, application.aggregate, presentation.display].
verification: Layer check: every declared JTBD step's primary layer(s) must equal the canonical layers-by-step value for that step (the bracketed list in each canonical routing row).
Sequence check: every declared call sequence must match the canonical sequence-by-step table for that step; comparison is ordered and exact per token.

No mechanical detector: compliance is reviewer/LLM-judged by checking every declared JTBD step for layers and sequence against the canonical step table. A step missing routing entirely is a finding, not out of scope.
Findings this check reports: a declared step without primary layer(s) or call sequence; a declared sequence that is not the canonical one (ordered, per-token).

The file-kind and phase facts are discovery hints only — not scope restrictions and not prerequisites: the rule applies to a JTBD step declaration in any artifact and in any phase; a phase observer would only help prioritise.

fires: A JTBD step (e.g. resolve) is declared or assigned in any artifact and no primary layer or call sequence is stated for it yet.
A plan artifact lists JTBD steps but omits a step's primary layer or gives a sequence that differs from the canonical one.
A reviewer checks a plan artifact containing JTBD steps to confirm each step is placed in the layered architecture.
doesNotFire: A coder implementing code inside one layer with no JTBD step being declared, assigned or reviewed.
Text that uses words like 'monitor' or 'define' in ordinary prose, not as a JTBD step.
Choosing or renaming the step taxonomy itself (governed by the JTBD taxonomy convention).

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's canonical layer roles, in dependency order with their local names, that JTBD steps are routed across and whose names are the only valid layer names in a step routing declaration.

The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role — the usual places where JTBD steps are declared. Used by the file-kind activation fact as a discovery hint only, never as a scope restriction: the rule applies to a JTBD step declaration in any artifact.

neutralityNotes: The canonical step→layers→sequence table is the convention's payload and is written entirely in the four canonical role names (presentation, application, domain, integration) plus methodology operation tokens, so it stays in the core verbatim; a stack whose local layer names differ supplies them via roles.layers (and roles.<role>.name), and the table is read against those roles — for Bun the local names equal the role names, so core + Bun profile impose the identical obligation. The concrete plan-artifact kind names (plan, product capability, desired outcome, planner_doc) are carried as profile data through roles.plan_artifact.kinds and expand the plan_artifact role of the file-kind discovery hint; 'acceptance' is a role-level kind kept in the core fact. Remaining Bun-only material: this rule's finding ids and verifier term ids (layers_by_step, sequence_by_step), and the sidecar's implementation metadata. The sibling-rule reference in doesNotFire was neutralized to 'the JTBD taxonomy convention' because rule ids are remapped per realization. The activation-fact notes (discovery hints, not scope restrictions or prerequisites) are preserved in core.verification because the neutral fact schema carries no note field.
